name: Ozone cupping

card.summary: A variant of cupping therapy in which ozone is introduced into the suction cups, offered with claims of better circulation and clearer-looking skin.
card.note: Cupping leaves bruise-like marks and can burn or scar skin; the FDA restricts medical claims for ozone.

quick.overview:
Ozone cupping combines two older practices: cupping, in which cups create suction on the skin, and ozone therapy, in which ozone gas is applied to the body. Practitioners who offer it describe it in terms of improved circulation and skin condition, which is where the appearance angle comes from.

It appears in classification lists of cupping types, where ozone is one of the materials placed inside the cups. Published research on this specific variant is not available; the surrounding fields have been reviewed separately.
quick.how: In cupping generally, cups are applied to the skin and left in place, sometimes slid across oiled skin. Ozone variants add ozone to the cup. Sessions are given by practitioners rather than self-administered.
quick.risks: Cupping can cause bruise-like marks, burns (especially with fire cupping), skin ulcers, darkening and scarring. Ozone therapy in other forms has caused serious harm, including deaths, and the FDA restricts its medical use. People with eczema or psoriasis are advised that cupping can worsen those conditions.

lead: Ozone cupping is a form of cupping therapy in which ozone is used inside the cups. A classification of cupping types by what is placed inside the cup lists ozone together with herbal products, water, moxa, needles and magnets. [1]

People interested in it for appearance generally have skin tone, circulation and complexion in mind. Practitioners of cupping in general claim benefits for acne, psoriasis and removal of stagnant blood or vital energy. [1]
Cupping reviews report poor-quality evidence overall, and ozone therapy is regulated or restricted in several countries. [1][2]

chain: Suction cups are placed on the skin with ozone introduced
Practitioners say circulation and skin condition improve
angle.text: Providers describe it as a way to improve circulation and skin condition. Those effects are claims from practitioners; the visible result of any cupping is bruise-like marks that fade over days.

paras: Cupping has been used since antiquity: wet cupping appears in Iranian traditional medicine and the work of Hippocrates, and the earliest Chinese record is from Ge Hong (281-341 AD). Hospitals in China have used it as a traditional modality since the 1950s. [1]
Ozone therapy introduces ozone or ozonides into the body by various routes. Ozone was used to disinfect operating rooms in 1856 and tested on wounds in World War I. [2]

No studies found on ozone cupping specifically. For cupping in general, reviews from 2011 and 2014 described poorly documented effectiveness and weak study design, and the American Cancer Society states that available evidence does not support claims of health benefits; some reviews find low to moderate evidence for musculoskeletal pain relief that may not differ from placebo. [1] For ozone therapy in general, the evidence for most proposed uses is limited. [2]
Cupping can leave bruise-like marks, burns, skin ulcers, darkening, scarring and pain, and the NCCIH notes it can worsen eczema or psoriasis. [1]

Ozone therapy by injection or infusion has been associated with serious adverse events including embolism, pulmonary edema and deaths. The FDA prohibits medical uses of ozone lacking proof of safety and effectiveness, Malaysia banned it in 2017, and Brazil legalized it as a complementary treatment in 2023. [2]

timeline.event: Ozone is first used to disinfect operating rooms. [2]
Chinese hospitals begin using cupping as a traditional-medicine modality. [1]
Brazil legalizes ozone therapy as a complementary treatment. [2]
